verdict.rationale: Square's own marketing says sellers can "set custom rules and alerts to manage risk" for online payment fraud. That is a first-party, user-defined rule that acts on payment events, but it covers only the risk/fraud domain and gets a single thin mention. Webhooks (event notification subscriptions) are developer building blocks for constructing automation, not a rules engine, so they earn no credit here. Missing for 10: general-purpose event-to-action rule definition beyond fraud, documentation of which triggers and actions are available, any AI-native or natural-language rule authoring, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
